Subject: Paper Use Review for the Third Reporting Period
Dear Department Heads,
When the review opened, figures were to be collected for two reporting periods only. The finance committee has now asked that a third period be recorded before any conclusions are drawn. Support for that period has been assigned in the same way as before, with each department's change between the first two periods measured against the company-wide target of a fifteen percent reduction per staff member. The code each department received as a result is shown in the attached record.
A resource adviser will visit each department marked Code 1 and will propose changes to its printing practices. Each department marked Code 2 must instead put forward one staff member for a two-hour session on printer settings, and I would ask you to send me the name by November 21. Departments marked Code 3 need take no further action.
Apart from these follow-up actions, any department may ask to have its desk printers replaced with shared printers. Requests must reach my office by November 7.
Thank you for your attention to this.
Bernard Kaminski
Office Services Manager
Extension 218
Records for the first two periods are held by Records Management.
----------------------
Paper Use Review: Recorded Figures by Department
Department	First period	Second period	Change	Action code
Human Resources	1,180	1,110	-6%	Code 2
Marketing	1,460	1,200	-18%	Code 3
Records Management	940	830	-12%	Code 2
Research	620	600	-3%	Code 1
Code 1 - reduction of less than 5 percent
Code 2 - reduction of 5 to 14 percent
Code 3 - reduction of 15 percent or more
Note: Figures are sheets of paper per staff member, not department totals. Departments are listed alphabetically.
----------------------
Paper Review Extended to a Third Period
Departments learn what the coming months will require of them
By Yolanda Brennan, staff writer
November 14
The paper-use review, which was to close at the end of this month, will now run through one further reporting period. Figures for the first two periods reached department heads in October, along with the follow-up action assigned to each department.
In Marketing the latest change has been an equipment one. "The desk printers are gone," said Felix Tolliver, the senior manager responsible for marketing. "Two shared printers arrived last week, and people collect their work in one trip." Printing of drafts, he added, had already been cut back sharply.
Doreen Vasquez, who directs the company's research work, said her own figures had barely moved. "Outside reviewers still ask us for paper copies of every report," she explained.
The recorded figures for all departments are posted outside the mail room.

Departments learn what the coming months will require of them

November 14
The paper-use review, which was to close at the end of this month, will now run through one further reporting period. Figures for the first two periods reached department heads in October, along with the follow-up action assigned to each department.

Dear Ms. Quintero:
I am writing to confirm that your annual service visit is booked for Tuesday, March 14, with arrival between 8:30 A.M. and 9:00 A.M. The attached work order lists every machine by its machine code.
During the visit, a temporary machine is placed on the floor only for a unit whose recorded monthly volume is above the allowance of 20,000 pages. Other machines are serviced in place and are out of use for about two hours.
To prepare for our visit, the equipment coordinator for each floor must send us a meter reading for every machine on that floor by the day before the visit. A machine with no reading does not reach the printed order. Coordinators are also asked to clear the space around each machine before our technician arrives. Should a machine be missing from the order, an addition may be requested by telephone at any point, subject to the technician's remaining time on the day of the visit.
Gordon Salgado
Service Scheduling Supervisor
Equipment Care Department
Winslow Business Machines | Account DI-2087
----------------------

Visit date	Tuesday, March 14

EQ-215	Floor 2, Room 2A	A2	Yes
EQ-232	Floor 2, Room 2E	A1	Not required

A1	Routine service only

March 14

Daniel Whitford

Sedgefield Conference Services | Registration Support
Attendee Changes: Trade and Industry Forum
This page is for anyone who holds a paid place at this year's Trade and Industry Forum, with or without a workshop seat, and can no longer attend. Fees are not refunded, and no places remain for sale. Rather than leave the seat empty, you may name a colleague to attend in your place. --[1]--
Naming Someone Else
The person you name must work for the same organization as you. --[2]-- Your request must reach us at least seven days before the opening day. Requests sent more than thirty days ahead carry a handling fee of $20. Requests sent later carry a fee of $45. --[3]-- Neither fee includes workshop bookings.
Requests arriving inside the final seven days cannot be accepted. --[4]-- Please send it to the support address below.
What the New Attendee Receives
The person replacing you takes over the main program sessions and the daily lunches in your booking. Two kinds of extras are treated differently. Workshop seats and evening dinner tickets stay with your own booking and must be reserved again by your replacement.
Common Questions
May I name someone from another company?
No. Only a colleague from your own organization qualifies.
Will a workshop seat be held for my replacement?
No. Seats are limited, and we cannot promise that a free one remains.
Page reference PG-2065
Last reviewed March 3
Registration support: support@sedgefieldconf.example

Group thread: Ridgeway session travel — Wednesday
Estelle Nowak [Payroll], 4:02 P.M.: Five of us are booked for Friday's planning session, under our department code TL-52. The site is the Millbank Center on Ridgeway Drive. Ruth is one of the five, though she is out today. It starts at 9:00, and the sign-in desk closes at 8:30. Instead of five cars, could we share?
Bruno Escalante [Shipping], 4:05 P.M.: Happy to drive, and we can settle up on fuel afterward. Who needs a place — all four of you, or just Ruth and Lucia? Once the stops are fixed, I'll send everyone a map of them.
Owen Halloran [Quality], 4:10 P.M.: Here are the stops I'd suggest:
— West entrance of our building, 7:15
— Grange Road bus stop, 7:25
— Train station taxi stand, 7:35
Lucia Ferraro [Design], 4:12 P.M.: That first one is cutting it close, isn't it?
Estelle Nowak [Payroll], 4:14 P.M.: You're right. The drive runs about seventy-five minutes at that hour, so there would be nothing left over. Let's move every stop up by half an hour.
Bruno Escalante [Shipping], 4:14 P.M.: Writing this before I saw your last message — my car takes four people in all, so one of us is left without a place.
Owen Halloran [Quality], 4:17 P.M.: I had already driven that stretch once last spring, when I took a load of sample cases out to the same address, so I'll follow in my own car.
Lucia Ferraro [Design], 4:19 P.M.: Then put me with Owen. I'd rather not squeeze into the back.
Estelle Nowak [Payroll], 4:22 P.M.: Good. Bruno takes Ruth and me, Owen takes Lucia. The Millbank lot admits no vehicle without a pass, though, and requests must be in by 5:00 the day before. Owen, could you file ours?
Owen Halloran [Quality], 4:24 P.M.: I'm on the floor all morning tomorrow and won't get to a computer. Lucia, would you take it?
Lucia Ferraro [Design], 4:26 P.M.: I'll do it. Send me both license plate numbers before four tomorrow and I'll request the two passes. I can leave my own car in the staff lot behind our building overnight.
5 participants, 11 messages

questions.passage:
To: Claudia Zamora
From: Gerald Ibarra
Date: March 2
Subject: Fair contacts and follow-up order
Dear Claudia,
We came back from the two-day housewares fair at the Kelso exhibition center on Tuesday evening with forty-eight new contacts, the largest number any of our staff has brought back from a single event. The crates of display units traveled home on the same truck and have already been unpacked in the storeroom. A contact list that long means the trip paid for itself.
Our second production run of the lidded pantry containers is due to be completed on March 14, and shipments to distributors begin in that same week. Until then, only twelve demonstration units remain in the storeroom, and because one unit must be left with a customer at each first visit, the order in which we approach these contacts has to be fixed before the first calls are made. Please work through the contacts in this order:
1. Department store buyers who asked for a price list. Call these first, this week, and offer a demonstration at their store.
2. Regional distributors who took a catalog but gave no order estimate. Reach these second and ask how many units each of them would expect to take. The customer service desk is still logging inquiries from the fair, so keep your notes separate from theirs.
3. Independent gift shops. Write to these only after the distributors have replied and it is clear that demonstration units are still uncommitted.
Once all twelve units have been committed, place any remaining contacts on a hold list and tell them that a visit can be arranged as soon as the new units reach us.
Thank you,
Gerald Ibarra
Sales Manager, Gilford Housewares
P.S. Hugo Espinoza will have the contact cards from the fair typed into a single list by Thursday morning, so you will have everything in one place before the first calls.

To: All installation crews
From: Helen Mortimer, Installation Supervisor
Date: February 27
Subject: Completion images and billing
From Monday, March 6, closing out a job will include one new step: photographing the finished work at the customer's home and sending the images to the office.
The change comes after several accounts went unpaid for weeks over the past four months because customers questioned marks and missing pieces that we could not account for once the crew had left. Some of you have called this extra paperwork at the end of a long day, and I understand that, but we have nothing to show what we handed over. Every van already carries a tablet, so no new equipment is needed.
Each set must show the following:
[1] the whole row of units with every door and drawer closed
[2] the joint where the counter meets the wall
[3] the base panels along the floor
[4] the inside of one upper unit with its shelves in place
[5] the floor and walls beside the finished units
On jobs of more than twelve units, add a wide view from the opposite corner. A sample set has already been circulated to crew leaders.
The images must be uploaded before the van comes back in. The office cannot release the bill for a job until the record is on file, so a set that arrives the next morning holds up payment. Staff here will match each set to the invoice.
To begin with, the step applies for four weeks only to the three crews at the north yard, where Culver Timber Supply will keep delivering materials to each address as before. Crew leaders in that group will check every set before it is sent. When the four weeks are up, the remaining crews will hear from me about a short training session. If customers continue to raise questions after that, we may ask for a signature on site as well.
This notice is posted in the tool room. Each crew leader must add initials beside the crew number.

Bexley Waste and Recycling Services
Service Change Notice
Applies to the closure week of Monday, November 23 through Saturday, November 28
Notice reference: WS-214
Because of the holiday, our collection schedule for the week of November 23 has changed, and regular collections that week will take place on replacement dates. Customers can find their new date by looking up their service area in the table below, which also shows when crews will arrive and any note on how containers should be handled.
Service area	Usual collection day	Replacement collection date	Crew arrival window	Container note
Fenmore	Monday	Tuesday, November 24	6:00 A.M. to 11:00 A.M.	Mixed recycling taken on the same visit
Longmead	Tuesday	Wednesday, November 25	6:00 A.M. to 11:00 A.M.	Cardboard must be flattened and tied
Stapleton	Thursday	Wednesday, November 25	12:00 noon to 4:00 P.M.	Food waste bins emptied separately
Holbeck	Thursday	Saturday, November 28	7:00 A.M. to 12:00 noon	Glass must be kept in a separate container
Petersham	Friday	Saturday, November 28	12:00 noon to 4:00 P.M.	Carts kept in a shared yard must be labeled
One further requirement applies to every customer. During the closure week, containers must be at the collection point by 5:30 A.M., one hour earlier than the usual deadline, and crews will not return to a site that sets out late.
Material left beside a container counts as additional volume and is charged at the standard extra-volume rate. This charge is waived for premises on the year-round collection plan but is applied in full to premises on the seasonal plan.
Customers who need an added visit during the closure week should send their request to the service line at least three business days in advance. Where the collection vehicle cannot reach a site's usual point, the route coordinator will contact that site before the replacement date.
Service line: 555-0197. Replacement dates are also posted at bexleywaste.example.

Sincerely,
Andre Sorensen
Route Coordinator, Holbeck and Petersham routes
Direct line: 555-0163

Dunmore Mailing Services
Print and Mail Production Department
Job reference BM-6704 — March 14
Attention: Mailing Coordinator, Pelham Garden Supply
Subject: Returned pieces from the spring catalog mailing
Dear Mailing Coordinator,
The spring catalog mailing was finished on March 6, and all 12,400 pieces were mailed that day. Since then, 187 pieces have come back to our plant as undeliverable. They are being held here, and we cannot send any of them out again until replacement address records arrive from your office.
The held pieces fall into three groups: incomplete address, no longer at this address, and refused by recipient. The list we mailed to you on March 11 records every returned piece separately, with its group and the name printed on the label, so that each entry can be matched against your own customer file.
Pieces in the incomplete address group are remailed at no charge, provided the corrected records reach us by March 27. Pieces in the remaining two groups are remailed at 58 cents each, because the address supplied to us was printed exactly as it was given at the time of production.
Corrected records contain your customers' personal details, so the resubmission form may be filed only by a member of your staff who has completed our data handling briefing and has been issued a briefing reference number. That number must appear on the form. Records that arrive after March 27 will be handled as a new mailing.
We are also able now to compare a client's whole address file with the national change-of-address register before printing begins, and clients who use that comparison see far fewer pieces come back. Please call my extension if you would like the fee for it.
Sincerely,

questions.passage:
Larchmont Property Care — Winter Clearing Register
Registered properties are cleared overnight without a single telephone call.
How enrollment works
1. Send us the enrollment form with the address of every entrance and parking area you want covered.
2. A supervisor walks the property with your staff, marks the lines our machines will follow, and places the equipment described below.
3. When the gauge at our office records two inches of snow, every registered property is cleared before six in the morning. No telephone call is needed.
Every registered property keeps two covered containers of de-icing salt, a mounted scoop, and a set of edge markers for its walkways. This equipment stays on the premises all season and remains ours. The containers are refilled every ten days from late November onward, whether or not the register has been activated. A supervisor also inspects each property once a month during the season.
Enrollment for this season closes on November 15. A preparation visit completed on or before that date is included at no charge. Visits completed later are billed at the standard hourly rate.
Weekdays: 555-0142. Written questions: register@larchmontcare.example
----------------------

Item	Location on site	Count	Status

Mounted scoop	Loading dock wall	1	Installed
Edge markers	Main entrance walkway	14	Set
Boundary markers	Delivery lane	6	Set
Drain covers cleared	Front curb	3	Completed
Exception: the gate to the north walkway was locked during the visit, so its markers were not set. To be completed on a later call.
Crew Leader: Simon Pascoe
Site Representative: Angela Hutchings
----------------------
Angela Hutchings, site manager, Kirkfield Business Court — first season on the register
The register was activated for the first time last Thursday. Snow started after ten at night, and when I arrived at half past seven the rear lot and the main entrance walkway were clear and treated. The crew leader had telephoned me at five in the morning to confirm that the work was done. Nobody from our office called anyone.
I raised one point during the preparation visit in November that is still open. Our tenants use the north walkway before the main entrance opens, and the gate to it was locked when the crew came, so its markers were never set. The record lists that as unfinished, and I would like it settled before the next snowfall.
Verdict: dependable, and best arranged well before the season begins.

To: All floor wardens, Denholm Place
From: Building Operations
Date: March 9
Subject: Staged evacuation exercise, March 20
Reference: EV-1450 — action required by every warden
To all floor wardens:
Two tenant firms have taken additional space since December, and far more people now work on the second and fourth floors than when the present stairway assignments were drawn up. The exercise on March 20 will show whether those assignments still empty the building within the eight-minute target. The exercise required each year under our safety certificate was completed in October, so this run is an additional one.
Each warden clears the areas listed against their zone and then leaves by the stairway shown on the attached sheet. Zones move in the order of the start times printed there, and no group should enter a stairway ahead of its own slot.
Reminder: the standing exception for Zone C applies to this run as well. Its wave begins after the other three so that visitors attending courses can be given instructions before they are moved.
Yvette Twomey will observe from the ground floor and will time each wave. Please hand her your completed zone tally within one business day. Her report will decide whether any assignment is changed before the next run.
Duncan Mulvaney
Operations Manager
Building Operations
Attachment: allocation sheet EV-1450, Revision 2
----------------------
Exercise: staged evacuation, practice run
Sheet reference: EV-1450
Prepared by: Building Operations
Revision: 2, issued with the exercise directive
Zone	Areas covered	Warden	Start	Stairway	Assembly point	Expected occupancy
A	Reception level and mail room	K. B.	10:00	East Stair	Front Plaza (2)	40
B	Second-floor open offices	P. R.	10:02	North Stair	Rear Yard	96
D	Fourth-floor call center	S. V.	10:04	South Stair	Front Plaza (2)	62
C	Third-floor training rooms and file room	T. N.	10:09 (1)	East Stair	Side Court	34
1. Later start approved for this zone so that course visitors are given instructions before they move.
2. Zones A and D use the same assembly point; wardens are to keep the two groups apart while counts are taken.
----------------------
Observation report — sheet EV-1450, run of March 20
Observer role: timekeeper and independent observer
Vantage point: ground-floor lobby desk, then the rear yard gate
Three of the four waves ran as allocated. The reception level and mail room group left the floor inside its slot, and the name list it handed in was complete and correct. The fourth-floor call center group was standing at its assembly point well before the end of its interval, the widest margin of the four groups. The third-floor training rooms and file room group began at the approved later time and finished inside its interval.
Movement was held up in two places. The second-floor group set off promptly, but the North Stair carried an unbroken line from the second floor to the ground for almost the whole interval, and the last of the group reached the yard about three minutes past its allocated time. On the East Stair, the ground-floor door was propped open only after the first group using that stair had reached it, which cost that group about forty seconds.
For the next run, the second-floor zone should be divided between the North Stair and the East Stair, with the two halves starting a minute apart.
Y. T.

questions.passage:
Brackenridge Energy Services
Workplace Energy Review
Brackenridge Energy Services carries out workplace energy reviews at no charge, showing businesses where their premises could use less gas and electricity.
To enter, send us the entry form with twelve months of meter readings, and we will confirm your place within three business days. Our survey team of two then spends one day on site, guided by a member of your staff. Four weeks after the visit, we mail you a written summary ranking the measures we recommend.
We can review premises only if their meters are registered in your name, not billed through a landlord or shared supply. You must also have occupied them for two years or more, and they must remain in use for a year after the visit. Each company may enter one property per round. Our team can also write an action plan on site for an optional $250.
Each round has its own entry deadline and review week:
Entries by March 6 — review week of April 13
Entries by May 1 — review week of June 8
brackenridgeenergy.example
----------------------
To: Ms. Fiona Steadman
From: Gavin Lindqvist
Sent: February 27, 10:12 A.M.
Subject: Energy review — site screening (WR-118)
Copy: Site Services file
Dear Ms. Steadman,
Brackenridge Energy Services reviews one property per company in each round, so only one site can be entered this round.
I have checked our four premises against the published conditions. Gas and electricity at Netherby Road are included in the rent we pay the landlord, as they have been since we took that unit. Bramley Lane is metered in our own name, though we moved in last April. Vine Street has had its own meters for years, but the building returns to its owner in September. Torrance Park has been ours since 2016, its meters are in our name, and the lease there runs to 2032.
The entry form calls for twelve months of meter readings. For the site I have in mind, the earlier readings sit with our former billing agent, and the March cutoff is one week away. I would therefore aim at the following round. Should the optional action plan be included?
Gavin Lindqvist
Facilities Coordinator, Site Services
Talbot Packaging
Extension 2140
----------------------
From: Fiona Steadman
Date: February 27, 1:45 P.M.
To: Gavin Lindqvist
Subject: Re: Energy review — site screening (WR-118)
File the entry against the March cutoff, not the later one. Our annual inventory count begins at Vine Street on May 18, runs through June, and will occupy this department, so the survey should be finished before it begins. Telephone the former billing agent's accounting office for the readings, which is quicker than writing.
This year's facilities budget carries nothing for outside consulting fees, so keep us to what the program provides. Once the entry has gone in, obtain written confirmation that our place is held.
F. S.
For internal circulation only.

questions.passage:
Brackenridge Energy Services
Workplace Energy Review
Brackenridge Energy Services carries out workplace energy reviews at no charge, showing businesses where their premises could use less gas and electricity.
To enter, send us the entry form with twelve months of meter readings, and we will confirm your place within three business days. Our survey team of two then spends one day on site, guided by a member of your staff. Four weeks after the visit, we mail you a written summary ranking the measures we recommend.
We can review premises only if their meters are registered in your name, not billed through a landlord or shared supply. You must also have occupied them for two years or more, and they must remain in use for a year after the visit. Each company may enter one property per round. Our team can also write an action plan on site for an optional $250.
Each round has its own entry deadline and review week:
Entries by March 6 — review week of April 13
Entries by May 1 — review week of June 8
brackenridgeenergy.example
----------------------
To: Ms. Fiona Steadman
From: Gavin Lindqvist
Sent: February 27, 10:12 A.M.
Subject: Energy review — site screening (WR-118)
Copy: Site Services file
Dear Ms. Steadman,
Brackenridge Energy Services reviews one property per company in each round, so only one site can be entered this round.
I have checked our four premises against the published conditions. Gas and electricity at Netherby Road are included in the rent we pay the landlord, as they have been since we took that unit. Bramley Lane is metered in our own name, though we moved in last April. Vine Street has had its own meters for years, but the building returns to its owner in September. Torrance Park has been ours since 2016, its meters are in our name, and the lease there runs to 2032.
The entry form calls for twelve months of meter readings. For the site I have in mind, the earlier readings sit with our former billing agent, and the March cutoff is one week away. I would therefore aim at the following round. Should the optional action plan be included?
Gavin Lindqvist
Facilities Coordinator, Site Services
Talbot Packaging
Extension 2140
----------------------
From: Fiona Steadman
Date: February 27, 1:45 P.M.
To: Gavin Lindqvist
Subject: Re: Energy review — site screening (WR-118)
File the entry against the March cutoff, not the later one. Our annual inventory count begins at Vine Street on May 18, runs through June, and will occupy this department, so the survey should be finished before it begins. Telephone the former billing agent's accounting office for the readings, which is quicker than writing.
This year's facilities budget carries nothing for outside consulting fees, so keep us to what the program provides. Once the entry has gone in, obtain written confirmation that our place is held.
F. S.
For internal circulation only.

Trade Store Adds Space in Two Stages
By Frances Ibarra, Pemberton
Thurlow Trade Supply is enlarging its Pemberton outlet in two stages, with a temporary entrance in use until the work ends.
The store occupies most of a two-level converted warehouse. Bulk orders sit on the upper level, which staff reach by a freight elevator shared with the sign-making workshop that rents the rest of that level; customers wait at the counter while items are carried down. --[1]--.
Construction of the extension is under way and will continue for about two months. The contractor counter and the lumberyard stay open throughout. --[2]--. While the work continues, deliveries and customer pickups both use a temporary gate at the rear of the yard, as the main vehicle entrance is closed. --[3]--.
The first stage, which opens on March 3, adds tool and fastener aisles on the extension's ground floor. Only holders of a Thurlow trade account may enter the new aisles at that stage, and account numbers will be checked at the aisle entrance. A second contractor counter and an indoor paint mixing area will follow in the second stage, from April 14, and the extension is open to every customer from that date. --[4]--.
Questions about site access may be sent to the store's order desk.

Site Administration Office, Wingate Place
Effective from March 2
Notice WP-4109
Confirmation on Arrival Now Required for Shared Meeting Rooms
During February, records showed that reserved rooms were repeatedly left empty for their full period while requests from other tenants for those same hours could not be met. For this reason, a tenant holding a reservation must now confirm it on arrival, within the time allowed for the length of the booking in the table below.
Length of booking	Confirmation deadline after scheduled start
Two hours or less	10 minutes
More than two hours	20 minutes
A reservation not confirmed by the deadline shown above is canceled automatically, and the time released is offered at once to the next tenant waiting for that room. During a January trial of this practice, such time was claimed within minutes. Rooms that have become free for the current day are also shown on the availability screen in the main lobby.
Tenants will continue to make and change reservations for the six shared meeting rooms on the fourth floor only through the online booking system. A reservation may not be transferred to another tenant company or occupant, and no tenant may hold more than two rooms for the same hour. In addition, reservations may not be entered more than four weeks in advance.
Questions may be sent to the Site Administration Office at extension 118.

Home / Account Help / Time Away
Time Away From Your Workspace
Members who will be away for several weeks do not have to end their agreement. Loxley Workspace lets you pause billing for a set number of days each membership year. Paid days you do not use are not refunded. Instead, they are added to the end of your current term. The option is open to members whose payments are up to date.
Plan level	Maximum suspended days per membership year*
Flex Desk	14
Reserved Desk	30
Private Office	45
*Suspended days must be taken in blocks of at least 5 and no more than 20 consecutive days.
How to request a pause
1. Sign in and open the Membership tab, then choose Pause Membership. Your request must be received at least 10 days before your next billing date.
2. Enter the first and last day of your planned absence. The dates you enter must meet the block limits shown above.
3. Submit the request and wait for our written confirmation, which is sent within three business days.
Members who do not use the website may instead ask front desk staff to file a request for them.
Please note: While your membership is suspended, your entry card remains active during staffed reception hours, and letters and parcels are still accepted at the front desk. Reception is staffed Monday through Friday. Conference-room credits do not build up during a suspension and cannot be used. Billing restarts on the day after the suspension ends.
Last reviewed: March. Related page: Moving your membership to another location.

1. Sign in and open the Membership tab, then choose Pause Membership. Your request must be received at least 10 days before your next billing date.
2. Enter the first and last day of your planned absence. The dates you enter must meet the block limits shown above.
3. Submit the request and wait for our written confirmation, which is sent within three business days.
Members who do not use the website may instead ask front desk staff to file a request for them.
Please note: While your membership is suspended, your entry card remains active during staffed reception hours, and letters and parcels are still accepted at the front desk. Reception is staffed Monday through Friday. Conference-room credits do not build up during a suspension and cannot be used. Billing restarts on the day after the suspension ends.

MEMO
To: Theresa Amundsen, Production Assistant
From: Lydia Mattison, Staff Placement Office, Danvers Company
Date: April 22
Subject: Work schedule change request WV-3086
This memo responds to the work schedule change request form you submitted on April 14. Under company policy, changes of this kind are open only to employees with at least one year of service, and after confirming that you qualify, this office has approved your request as a trial of three months rather than the six months you proposed. The terms of the trial are as follows:
Current schedule: five days, Monday through Friday, 8:30 A.M. to 4:30 P.M.
Approved schedule: four days, Monday through Thursday, 7:30 A.M. to 5:30 P.M.
Start date: June 1
Trial length: three months
In your form, you explained that the fabric dyeing line runs in long batches, so a ten-hour day would let you carry each batch from vat filling to drying without handing it over, and that you need the fifth day for family commitments. You also described how your work will be covered. On Fridays, a colleague on the same line will take the vat readings and move finished rolls on the loading elevator shared by all tenants, while work coats will continue to go out with the contracted laundry service. The only document attached to your form was a written agreement signed by that colleague. No medical statement was included, and none is required for a request of this kind.
Please note that the change will begin on June 1 only if the colleague's signed agreement remains on file with this office, and that your workstation will be listed for shared use on Fridays only. This office will notify the payroll section of your new hours. Since your supervisor was consulted on April 9 and your Friday coverage is already arranged, you will need to take just one step yourself: before your first four-day week, enter your new hours in the online timekeeping record. Your schedule will be reviewed on September 8, when a written schedule confirmation will be issued.

Ingleby Grocery
17 Fordyce Road, Hartwell

Dear Ms. Alvarado,
Our records show that your premises hold two separate annual authorizations, a retail sales permit and a sidewalk display permit. From the coming renewal cycle, these two permits will be combined into a single yearly business license, and one renewal will cover both activities.
The two permits have run on separate schedules since the store first opened, and each has required its own form. Please complete the enclosed renewal form and return it to this office by November 15. The fee basis is unchanged, so the amount you pay will be the same as last year. The file code shown above stays with your record and should be written on the form.
Holders may now elect a three-year term in place of the standard one-year term. This choice is available only where the record carries no unpaid charge and no open inspection item. Payment by monthly installment will not be offered. As in past years, a reminder notice will be mailed to you before your license expires.
You need not surrender your current certificates. Keep them on display until the new license reaches you. Questions about any entry on the form may be sent to this office at the address above.
Sincerely,
Yolanda Pike
Supervisor, Permits and Registrations Unit
Enclosure: consolidated license renewal form
P.S. The two former permit forms will be withdrawn on December 1. Any renewal submitted on them after that date will be returned to you unprocessed.

Compact stores such as ours receive only part of the chain's product range, and the larger cooking equipment is placed with the full-size stores.

Sincerely,
Odette Marchetti

Ryecroft Skills Center: Arranging a Course Series
Quick links: topic list, room guide, invoices, programs desk
Employers may book instructor-led sessions for their own staff, while individual learners use our public enrollment page. An employer arranging a series of sessions for its staff should follow the three steps below.
1. Send an inquiry naming your subject and staff numbers.
2. Say how the staff are divided and which format each group needs. A seminar uses a classroom. A workshop needs a practical room, available at the Kestrel Street center but not at the Grantham Street annex.
3. A confirmed program with a booking reference follows within five business days.
Employer sessions begin at 6 P.M. or later on weekdays, since daytime rooms are kept for our own public courses. Employers who pay in advance are charged five percent less, and a single program of six sessions or more brings a printed handbook for each participant at no charge. Individual learners pay the listed price.
Page last reviewed in March. Other questions go to the programs desk.

PROGRAM NEWS
Category Panels Take Over the Awards Judging
By Bernard Tomlin, Members' Bulletin
For several years, every entry to the Alliance Awards was read by the same in-house committee at the association office. That committee now prepares the scoring guide only. Each award category is reviewed instead by a small group of people who put their names forward from member businesses. "A single committee could not read every entry with the care it deserved," said Yvette Bouchard, awards coordinator. "People who run a business judge these entries better than we did."
Every session opens with the chair going through the scoring guide with the panel, before any entry is opened. Entries are then scored one at a time, and each panel agrees on its shortlist before leaving the room.
The placements now posted are provisional. Checking of entries continues to the end of February, and a panel may still be altered where a category gains or loses entries. Volunteers are asked to confirm their attendance with the awards office by February 20.

Date: September 29
Subject: Meeting of September 30
Reference: Items 2 and 3
Good morning, Neil:
I cannot be at tomorrow's meeting. After 5:30 p.m. on Tuesdays I am alone in the shop, and I cannot leave before we close at 7:00 p.m. Owen Maddox, who runs the hardware store on Cleave Court, will speak for me instead. Regards,
Margaret Doyle
Owner, Ardley Stationery
14 Hensley Street, Havelock
----------------------
Late Shopping Evenings Draw Steady Crowds
By Janet Whelan, Local Business
Shops in central Havelock stayed open until 9:00 p.m. on two evenings last week, and the Havelock Retailers' Association reports steady visitor numbers.
"Thursday was busier than any Saturday this year, and most of those who came in had never visited us," said Arnold Deming, who runs a bookstore on Priory Lane.
The blocks did not open late on the evenings first announced. The South Block shops opened late on Wednesday, October 8, and the North Block on Thursday, October 9, the members having agreed to exchange the two dates.
The association, which meets on the last Tuesday of each month, has forty-one members, and thirty-four opened on one of the two evenings. Every participating shop appeared in a flyer delivered across the town, and the cost of printing and delivery was divided among them by storefront width. Officers say a further promotion is planned, but no date is fixed.

From: Miriam Escalante, Central Travel Desk
Date: February 5
Subject: Booking overnight accommodation
Dear colleagues,
Beginning March 2, overnight accommodation will no longer be arranged by individual travelers or by their departments. Every request will instead be placed by this desk on your behalf. --[1]--.
For each trip, the desk will select from the properties we hold under agreement, confirm the reservation, and have the room charge billed directly to the company account. You will therefore not pay for the room and claim the amount back afterward. --[2]--. Incidental charges such as meals and parking remain yours to settle at the property.
We currently hold agreements with properties in eleven cities. A number of client sites and smaller offices lie outside that list. --[3]--.
The agreed rates can be secured only if the desk receives your request at least ten business days before the first night. Requests that arrive later will be booked at whatever rate the property is offering that week.
For trips already scheduled in March, please send the dates, the destination, and the number of nights to the desk before February 16. --[4]--.
Miriam Escalante
Coordinator, Central Travel Desk
Reference code TR-905. Questions may be directed to extension 2140.

Tarrington Parks Division
Corley Park Evening Fitness Program
Posted: March 14
To: All enrolled participants
The evening fitness sessions continue on the schedule issued when you enrolled, on Tuesdays and Thursdays at 6:30 P.M. on the north lawn. Because the lawn cannot be used safely during heavy rain, a standing indoor arrangement now applies to those sessions. --[1]--.
A session is moved indoors whenever rain is falling at 4:00 P.M. on a session day. Light drizzle earlier in the day does not change the outdoor plan. --[2]--. On such evenings the group meets in Activity Room B at the park recreation building. That room holds 24 participants, considerably fewer than the lawn. --[3]--. Places are given in the order of arrival, and the door opens at 6:15 P.M. The mats and hand weights stored in the box beside the lawn are not brought to Activity Room B.
A session lost to rain is not repeated later in the season. --[4]--. The evening's status is announced by 4:30 P.M. on a recorded telephone line, 555-0143, and participants should confirm it there before traveling to the park. Individual telephone calls and messages are not sent.

East walkway repairs — Tuesday, March 4
Lidia Kubiak (10:52): Two shops on the east walkway called. Ferndale Books and Selby Coffee House both say the drilling drowns out conversation at their counters. The work has been quiet for two weeks, and another stage follows.
Julian Behrens (10:55): Which stage is Halvern running now?
Renata Vogel (10:58): I'm on the east walkway, and you can hear it from the upper concourse. They began the noisy part of stage three today, and the foreman wants any change to the start time from us in writing before he books the crew.
Julian Behrens (11:02): Then move that stage to before we open. We could also ask the shops to keep their connecting doors shut.
Lidia Kubiak (11:05): I am with you there. The doors are the shops' own call, though.
Renata Vogel (11:09): So far the shops here are the only ones affected. Halvern's notice at the site gate says stage three is lifting the worn tiles along the east walkway, and stage four is laying and sealing the replacement surface.
Julian Behrens (11:12): The stores open at 10:00 A.M., so the loud work must stop by 9:30. Our cleaning crew can go over the walkway before the doors open.
Renata Vogel (11:15): The foreman raised evening work, but Danforth Security locks the service entrance at 8:00 P.M. and cannot staff it later.
Lidia Kubiak (11:19): Julian, the shops are yours, a note under each door today. I will take care of the written notice for the foreman, and one of you confirm back to me before Thursday morning.

Ainsworth Manufacturing — Supplier Records Office
Approved Supplier List: Registration Categories
Page last revised: February 2
An outside business is entered on the approved supplier list under one of four registration categories. Each category covers a different kind of work and carries its own requirements, which are set out in the table below. Applicants should select the single category that matches the way their business operates.
Category	Work covered	Document required	Review period	Availability expected
Category A: Unscheduled repair work	Repairs to building equipment requested at short notice	Current certificate of liability insurance	Three weeks	Telephone answered at every hour of the day, and a worker able to reach the site on the day of the call
Category B: Scheduled servicing	Planned servicing of ventilation and heating equipment on a yearly calendar	Signed servicing-standards agreement	Four weeks	Visits booked at least one week ahead, with no calls accepted outside office hours
Category C: Parts and materials supply	Delivery of replacement parts and consumable materials to the central stockroom	Current product price list	Ten business days	Deliveries brought on weekdays between 8:00 A.M. and 4:00 P.M.
Category D: Inspection and testing	Annual safety inspections and equipment testing	Current certificate of liability insurance	Five weeks	Inspection dates agreed one month in advance
Completed forms, together with the document listed for the chosen category, should be sent to the Supplier Records Office by e-mail or by internal mail. A file that is missing a listed document is kept on record, and the review period shown for its category begins on the day that document reaches this office. Notice of the decision is sent to the applicant at the end of that period.
----------------------
To: Supplier Records Office, Ainsworth Manufacturing
From: Ivan Kowalski
Date: February 26
Subject: Registration as an approved supplier
Reference: VC-2185
Attachment: 1 file
Dear Supplier Records Office,
One of your maintenance supervisors suggested that I write to you after our crew repaired two heating units at your plant last month. I have since studied your category page and completed the form, which is attached.
Our telephone is never left unattended, and a technician can normally be at a customer's site a few hours after a call, weekends included. I would be glad of your confirmation that I have selected the right category for the work we do.
One document, however, is not yet in my hands. Our insurer is preparing a renewed certificate of liability insurance and expects to issue it in about ten days. Could you tell me whether the review period shown on your page starts when the form arrives or only when that certificate is received?
Sincerely,
Ivan Kowalski
Lindow Mechanical Services
Reference VC-2185
Enclosure: completed registration form, one page

Coburn Business Rewards — Catalog valid March 1 through May 31
A new catalog is issued every three months, and items are seldom carried over.
Reward category	Representative items	Credit required	Supply and handling
Office Furnishings	Desk chair, storage cabinet	12,000	Delivered by our own trucks on a weekday morning. A signature is required.
Business Technology	Tablet computer, portable projector	8,000	Shipped to the member directly by the manufacturer. Our branches do not hold these items.
Everyday Supplies Bundle	Copier paper and ink cartridges	6,000	Held in branch stockrooms; must be picked up within thirty days of approval.
Break Room Refreshments	Coffee machine, water dispenser	4,000	Held at the member's home branch for pickup.
Claim forms are held at every branch counter.
----------------------
To: Rewards Administration Desk, Coburn Office Supply
From: Rosemary Attwell
Date: April 14
Subject: Rewards balances at our two offices
Accounts concerned: RW-6314 (Eastgate office), RW-6320 (Ambleside office)
Copy: Branch Accounts Team
To the Rewards Administration Desk:
Our practice keeps a rewards account for each of its two offices. The Eastgate account shows 5,600 credits, of which 3,000 were awarded under the spring bonus offer rather than earned on purchases. The Ambleside account shows 2,600 credits, all earned on supply orders. Two years ago we claimed a coffee machine for the Eastgate break room.
Neither balance is large enough on its own, so I am asking that the two totals be brought together under the Eastgate account. Our records room could use the storage cabinet in the current catalog, though I expect that is beyond our reach. Otherwise we would like the single item of greatest value that our combined credit will cover.
Thank you for your assistance,
Rosemary Attwell
Office Manager, Lassiter Dental Group
Eastgate office
P.S. The Eastgate credit expires on May 31, so an early decision would help us.
----------------------
Combining Rewards Balances: Program Rules
For member businesses holding accounts at more than one branch.
A. Who may ask, and how
Both accounts must be registered to the same member business, and the request must be put in writing by the person named as the contact on each account. Requests from other staff are returned without action.
B. Credit that carries across
Credit earned on supply orders carries across in full. Credit awarded through a bonus offer carries across at half its value, and the reduction is applied before the two totals are added.
C. What a combined balance cannot buy
A combined balance may not be used for any category supplied by an outside company rather than from the program's own stock. Those items must be claimed against a single account.
D. Timing
Requests are settled within ten business days. Credit that expires during that period cannot be restored.
Questions may be sent to the Rewards Administration Desk.

questions.passage:
Product Development Notes
Home Panel Findings Lead to Two Design Changes
Two features of the cordless sweeper made by Hollingsworth Home Products were altered after the company's first home trial cycle closed in March.
The dust container on the sample unit was enlarged, and the power switch was moved from the body of the machine to the handle. Comments about the noise of the motor were also common, but the motor itself was left unchanged.
Ninety households took part, each using a preproduction unit for six weeks in place of its own cleaning equipment and filing three short written reports.
"A machine behaves differently in a home than it does in our testing rooms," said Nigel Braithwaite, who manages the panel program at the research office. "Neither change would have been made without the panel."
The cycle now under way differs in one respect. Members are being placed in two groups, and one group will keep its sample unit for twelve weeks instead of six.
Gwen Aldridge, contributing writer, Household Trade Review
[Figures supplied by the manufacturer's research office.]
----------------------
Subject: Home panel, cycle beginning in May
To: Lucia Moreno
From: Nigel Braithwaite
Date: May 2
Panel reference: HP-6402
Enclosed: Home Panel Reporting Schedule
Hello Ms. Moreno,
Your place on the current panel is confirmed, and everything you need for the coming weeks is set out below.
Your trial will run for twelve weeks rather than the usual six, so the unit is due back with us in early August.
The kit will reach you on May 5. It contains one sweeper, a spare filter, and a care sheet. The sweeper is the revised sample built after the first cycle, not the standard unit now sold in stores.
The enclosed schedule gives the reporting dates. Please read the rows marked for a longer trial as well as the rows that apply to everyone.
Please write back to confirm that a weekday delivery can be accepted at your address, as the courier will not hold the kit for a second day.
Nigel Braithwaite
Panel Coordinator
Research Office, Hollingsworth Home Products
Telephone extension 218
P.S. Please keep the shipping carton. You will need it to send the unit back at the end of the trial.
----------------------
Home Panel Reporting Schedule
Scope: applies to every member enrolled in the cycle beginning in May. Rows marked extended use apply only to members whose trial period runs for twelve weeks.
Round	Reporting window	Report covers	Attach with report
Round 1	May 12-18	First two weeks of use	No attachment
Round 2	June 2-8	Results on two types of floor	Two photographs of the unit in use
Round 3	June 16-22	Overall opinion of the unit	Completed condition checklist
Round 4 (extended use)	July 28 - August 3	Performance after long use	Battery charging log
1. Reports are entered on the member page of the company website. Paper reports are not accepted.
2. A member who misses a reporting window should telephone the research office, which will set a single replacement date.

Product Development Notes
Home Panel Findings Lead to Two Design Changes
Two features of the cordless sweeper made by Hollingsworth Home Products were altered after the company's first home trial cycle closed in March.
The dust container on the sample unit was enlarged, and the power switch was moved from the body of the machine to the handle. Comments about the noise of the motor were also common, but the motor itself was left unchanged.
Ninety households took part, each using a preproduction unit for six weeks in place of its own cleaning equipment and filing three short written reports.
"A machine behaves differently in a home than it does in our testing rooms," said Nigel Braithwaite, who manages the panel program at the research office. "Neither change would have been made without the panel."
The cycle now under way differs in one respect. Members are being placed in two groups, and one group will keep its sample unit for twelve weeks instead of six.
Gwen Aldridge, contributing writer, Household Trade Review

www.larkfieldpartnership.org/displaywindows
Display Windows for Local Makers
Who takes part
The program borrows shop windows that stand empty between tenants and fills them with work by makers based in the town. The categories change each season. Last season's round covered hand-bound books and woven baskets. This season the program is open to makers working in clay, glass, wood, or textiles.
How sites are allocated
Sites are grouped by window size, and makers who submit larger work are offered the wider windows. Each allocated site comes with one loaned fixture, listed in the site directory. The fixture stays in the window for the season and is returned to the office when the display closes.
Before you install
Every maker must attend one briefing session before any work is placed in a window. Makers holding Zone A sites attend on 6 March at Larkfield Market House. Makers holding Zone B sites attend on 8 March at Oxley Community Hall. Start times are sent by e-mail. Bring your allocation notice with you.
Send questions to the Window Program Desk, 18 Voss Street, or use the form on this page.
----------------------
To: Window Program Desk, Larkfield Town Center Partnership
From: Camille Batista
Sent: 24 February
Subject: Site DW-244
Attachment: allocation notice
Dear Window Program Staff,
Thank you for the notice confirming that site DW-244 on Mercer Street has been allocated to me for the coming season.
Each of my pieces is shaped on a wheel, left to dry for a week, and then baked at high heat twice, so the larger bowls are far heavier than they look. Could you tell me whether the fixture provided at my site will hold weight of that kind, or whether a stronger stand can be arranged instead?
I plan to attend the briefing session for my zone and would be grateful if you could confirm the start time. I print my own price cards and labels, so I can bring a set as a sample if that would help.
Regards,
Camille Batista
Batista Studio, Unit 3, Quarry Lane
www.camillebatista.com

Rating: 4 out of 5
Rental period: 9 weeks
Account type: Business (verified)
Posted: March 14
Nothing I read before booking told me where the limits of this arrangement lie, so I am setting them out here.
Our lease ended nine weeks before the new floor was ready, and buying desks we would then store would have cost more than renting. We took 24 pieces. Delivery staff removed the protective covers on arrival.
The desks and seating were sound. The three storage cabinets, though, were too shallow to hold our files upright. An exchange must be requested while at least fourteen days of the term remain, and we were inside that window, so I asked for deeper units. They arrived four days later rather than the next business day. I claimed nothing off the invoice and booked a second short rental in February.
The total came to $2,150, which our relocation budget covered easily, though delivery and pickup are billed separately and the rate list does not say so.
In my view, then, this kind of rental works well for short projects that need standard desks and seating, but it is a poor fit for teams with unusual storage needs or for terms of under three weeks.
Postings appear only after this site verifies an invoice.

Beckworth Art Supply
Celebrating Twenty Years on Halstead Street
Anniversary Week: Monday, June 8, through Saturday, June 13
For twenty years, painters, students, and hobbyists in this neighborhood have shopped at our counter, and we are grateful to every one of you. --[1]--.
A gift for you. During anniversary week, a commemorative pocket sketchbook showing our original storefront will be waiting at the front counter. Any purchase, of any size, entitles you to one, and we ask that each customer take only one copy. --[2]--.
Your work on our walls. From the first day of anniversary week, the long wall beside the front window, cleared when we moved our paper racks to the back of the store, will be given over to work by our customers. Our staff will mount every piece, so you need only bring the work in. Pieces may be no larger than 40 by 50 centimeters and must be unframed, since each one is held with clips, and all work must be handed in by Friday, June 5. The display will be taken down on Saturday, June 20, and pieces may be picked up at the counter from the following Monday. --[3]--.
Thank you for shopping with us, and we look forward to seeing your work. --[4]--.
The staff of Beckworth Art Supply

Group thread: Kelbrook sample intake
Tuesday, June 10
Marisol Cadena (1:40 P.M.): Merton Grill called. Their kitchen manager took four water samples at nine this morning and left them at our north unit instead of here. She needs results by Friday.
Tobias Ruiz (1:44 P.M.): Nothing came in from the grill on this morning's pickup round, so she must have left the box at the door. Graham, is it on your intake shelf?
Graham Purcell (1:49 P.M.): Found it at the back, with the grill's name on the lid.
Marisol Cadena (1:52 P.M.): Is a collection time written on the bottles?
Graham Purcell (1:55 P.M.): No, only the date. I'm at the north unit until six, and my next shift at the main site is tomorrow morning. The machine here is out for servicing, so nothing can be run at this end. I'll write the box up on the intake sheet once you decide.
Tobias Ruiz (1:58 P.M.): I could pick the box up on my four o'clock run and bring it over.
Graham Purcell (2:01 P.M.): One minute, someone's at the door.
Marisol Cadena (2:04 P.M.): That won't get us very far. Your run doesn't reach the main site until after five, and water that old tells us nothing.
Graham Purcell (2:07 P.M.): Back. Two conditions apply before we can accept water. First, it has to reach one of our sites within eight hours of being taken. Second, every bottle has to be sealed and marked with the time of collection. Neither applies here.
Marisol Cadena (2:12 P.M.): I'll ask for a fresh set first thing tomorrow, and mailing them is not an option.

To: Denise Voss
From: Martin Hale, Open Day Coordinator, Plant Office
Date: April 28
Subject: Your Family Open Day guest registration
Dear Ms. Voss,
Thank you for sending your guest details for the Foxley Engineering Company Family Open Day on Saturday, May 17. The four guests you have registered are listed below. This is the full number allowed for each employee; a fifth name would go on a waiting list, with the place confirmed by our office one week before the visit.
Guest name	Age group	Meal
Ruth Voss	12 and over	Standard
Peter Voss	12 and over	Vegetarian
Ida Voss	Under 12	Standard
Felix Voss	Under 12	Standard
To complete your registration, please sign the attached guest form and hand it in at the Plant Office by Friday, May 2. Forms sent by internal mail cannot be accepted. Once your form arrives, our staff will print badges for your guests and send your meal choices to the cafeteria.
A midday meal in the site cafeteria is included with every guest place at no charge, while printed group photographs are sold at the reception desk for $6 each. Please note that employee parking permits do not cover guest vehicles, so your guests should use the visitor spaces beside the main gate.
Although the assembly area is part of the standard tour, guests in the under-12 group may not enter it. Those guests will wait in the display room with you, and safety glasses will be lent at the assembly area entrance to the guests who go in. By signing the form, you accept responsibility for the conduct of your guests during the visit.
Sincerely,
Martin Hale
Open Day Coordinator, Plant Office

To: Mr. Douglas Peralta
From: Repairs Counter, Mowbray Works
Date: March 20
Subject: Result of your purchase protection claim
Claim reference: RC-5140
Thank you for leaving your machine with us on March 12 with your completed claim form. You mentioned then that you plan to travel to work on it each morning once it is returned.
The rear hub has failed and no longer turns freely. The rim above it is bent and several spokes are loose. The seat and the handlebar grips show ordinary wear only, and the helmet you left with the machine is undamaged. We forwarded our findings to the maker's support office, which has ruled that a hub failure of this kind falls inside the plan but impact damage to a rim does not. Your claim has therefore been decided in two parts, as set out below.
Covered by the plan: a new rear hub, supplied and installed at no charge.
Not covered by the plan: straightening the rim and replacing spokes, $58.00, of which $19.00 is labor.
Please approve the second line in writing before we begin the work. We can hold the machine for ten days. Without a reply by March 30, you will need to pick it up unrepaired.
The replacement hub came from our regional warehouse and is already here. Your purchase record was already on file, so we did not need to ask you for it. We will also check the seat height at no charge before the machine leaves us, and you will find our counter beside the luggage shop.
Ellis Karvonen
Repairs Counter, Mowbray Works
P.S. We will take care of the labor portion shown on the second line ourselves, as the machine has waited here longer than we promised.

Oakbourne Cleaning Services
Home | Services | Book a Visit | Contact
After-Hours Cleaning
Our after-hours service cleans the carpets and floors of shops and small offices while they are closed, so your business is never disturbed. To book a visit, send us a request at least seven days before the date you would like. In it, list each area to be treated, such as the sales floor, staff room, or offices, and name anything in each area that the crew must leave untouched.
Your request must also name one of our three visit times. Because each time comes with its own access arrangement, please choose the one that matches how your premises can be opened and locked.
6:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. — a member of your staff stays on the premises throughout
9:00 p.m. to 1:00 a.m. — a keyholder lets the crew in and returns at the end of the visit to lock up
4:00 a.m. to 8:00 a.m. — a set of keys is left at our office one business day beforehand
Finally, describe the entrance the crew will use, since it sets the arrival allowance, which is the time we set aside before work begins. A ground-floor door with parking beside it needs 15 minutes, while a door reached by stairs only, or one with parking more than 100 yards away, needs 45 minutes.
A few conditions apply to every booking. Our crews bring their own machines and water, so nothing needs to be supplied at the premises. After a visit, treated carpet must not be walked on for six hours. If your plans change, a booked date may be changed once, with three business days' notice.
----------------------
The late evening slot suited us
Rating: 5 out of 5 — service used: after-hours carpet cleaning
Colin Radcliffe, owner of a toy shop, Norbury district
Our shop closes at eight, and I did not want machines running around customers, so I chose the later evening time. I let the crew in myself at nine and came back at 12:30 to lock up after them. Our unit sits above a bakery and has no elevator, so the crew carried every machine up two flights from the street, and work on the carpet still began before ten.
They worked around the display shelves with real care, and nothing was marked. That is not the main reason we changed suppliers, though. The company we used last year told us to clear the floor ourselves before each visit, which kept two of my staff late the night before. This crew moves the furniture out and puts it back as part of the job.
Would book again: Yes

Bank	Unit size	Assigned to	Keys picked up from

Bank F, fourth floor, copier alcove	Full height	Staff on site every business day, floors 3-4	Staff entrance desk
Bank G, basement	Full height	Department equipment, one key per team	Staff Facilities Office

Staff who attend on set days only are paired, two holders to each half-height unit. In every case, no key is issued until the signed shared-use record for that unit has been handed in.
Cynthia Barlowe, who kept the holder register until February, has moved to the north site, so additions and changes now go to Beatrice Ndiaye.

To: All staff who claim work travel costs
From: Harriet Vance
Date: August 24
Subject: Entering your own travel costs
Attached: Staff Travel Payment Rates, Version 3
Dear colleagues,
From September 1, travel costs are entered by the traveler, and paper claim forms are no longer accepted.
Three steps apply. First, enter each journey on a separate line with its date, the way you traveled and the distance covered. Second, ask your supervisor to mark the line as agreed. Nothing is printed for signature, and no paper reaches this office. Third, use the attached sheet for the amount payable and for the kinds of travel that need a receipt.
A line is included in the following month's payment only if it is complete — entered, agreed and carrying any receipt required — by the 25th of the month. Payments are made in the second week of each month.
Questions to the extension below.
Harriet Vance
Employee Payments Office
Extension 4120
----------------------
Staff Travel Payment Rates — Version 3, in force from September 1
Travel category	Payment basis	Amount payable	Receipt required
Own car, self-driven	Per mile	32 cents*	No
Bicycle	Per mile	12 cents	No
Train or scheduled bus	Per journey	Ticket price	Yes
Taxi	Per journey	Meter fare**	Yes
* A journey longer than 50 miles is paid at 38 cents a mile for its whole distance.
** Payable only where this office agreed to the taxi beforehand. Without that agreement, only the train or bus amount is paid.
Rates are reviewed each January.
----------------------
To: Nina Whitfield
From: Lydia Steadman
Date: September 26
Subject: Your travel claim
Claim reference: TR-3096
Dear Ms. Whitfield,
Thank you for the four journeys entered under the reference above.

Visitor Information — Timed Entry to Light and Line
Admission to Light and Line is managed to protect the upper gallery, which holds only a set number of visitors at one time. Entry to the exhibition is included in regular museum admission, and no extra payment is collected at the gallery door. Every visitor, museum members included, must hold a reservation for a specific entry time before arriving, and reservations are made in advance at rothwellmuseum.org. Before booking, please review the details below.
Exhibition run: March 4 through June 21
Entry times: every 20 minutes from 10:00 A.M. to 4:20 P.M.
Places per reservation: 6 maximum
Advance booking: members may reserve from February 3, and all other visitors from February 17
Parties of 12 or more: a separate group arrangement is required
Entry times in the middle of the day are taken quickly, so visitors whose plans allow it should choose an early morning or a late afternoon time. Visitors who find no suitable time online still have another option. A small number of same-day places are issued at the Lobby Information Desk in the main hall from 9:45 A.M. each day, and these places are not offered through the website.
For a group arrangement, write to groups@rothwellmuseum.org. For help with seating, wheelchairs, or listening equipment, call 555-0188.

From: Joyce Tanaka, Learning Programs Coordinator
To: All Head Office Staff
Date: February 18
Subject: Student Visit Week, March 23-27
Dear Colleagues,
Last year's Student Visit Week was well received by the students from Dunmore Technical College and by the employees who took part, and the college has asked to send a second group in March. Fourteen students will attend, and one host is needed for each. This program is separate from the in-house Supervisor Skills course, which continues as scheduled.
The students will be on site from 9:30 A.M. until 3:30 P.M. each day. Passes will be issued at the sign-in counter on the ground floor on Monday morning, and hosts should meet their assigned student there before going up to the team work areas. Hosts will receive a short briefing in the third-floor training room the previous Thursday, and one midday meal in the staff dining area is provided. Every host is also asked to write a few lines at the end of each day, and these notes will shape the plan for next year's group.
Staff who wish to take part can choose from three levels of commitment. A full-week host keeps one student from Monday to Friday and sets a task each morning. A two-day host shares one student with a second host on any two days, while a single-day host takes one student for just one day. Please note that no more than three hosts per team can be accepted.
To take part, send me a short message stating which option you have chosen, no later than Friday, March 6. Your team leader's agreement must already be in place, as that cannot be arranged through this office.
Thank you for your help.
Joyce Tanaka
Learning Programs Coordinator
Internal extension 418

Changes Ahead at Renshaw Stationers
Local Business Section — By Ian Furlong
Millbrook, May 2
Frances Duvall, who opened Renshaw Stationers and has directed it ever since, will step back from daily management at the end of this month. Two members of her staff, Grace Abbott and Emil Kovacs, will take on the business jointly from June 1.
The store began in 1981 as a counter at the back of a printing company and has operated from its present address on the town's main business street for more than forty years. It supplies notebooks, file folders, and desk equipment to local offices and to schools across the district.
Ms. Abbott began as a delivery driver and now keeps the accounts, while Mr. Kovacs has taken orders at the front counter for eighteen years. Staffing will remain as it is. "The name above the door will not change, and neither will the way we do business," Mr. Kovacs said.
The store will close on May 18 while new shelving is installed inside, and it will reopen at the same address on May 26. Orders may be placed by e-mail throughout the closure, with no charge added for delivery. Deliveries themselves begin again on the reopening day, and a customer who needs an order before then may pick it up from the company's storage unit on Kestrel Lane.
Ms. Duvall will keep an office upstairs two mornings a week until December. "I would rather leave the store to people who helped build it than to a stranger," she said. "Our nine employees are all staying, and the work goes on as before."

questions.passage:
Annual Comparison
Small-Office Copiers: How This Year's Ratings Were Made
Four submitted units, one rating still unfinished.
By our equipment testing editor, Naomi Pilcher
Four criteria decide the standing. Running cost per page carries the greatest weight, followed by output quality, then speed, then reliability in daily use. Last year speed came first, but readers told us that running costs matter more, so the order was changed for this cycle. Each criterion is placed in one of three bands, excellent, good, or fair, and the standard program runs ten weeks.
The LP-620 reached our test office eleven days after the testing period had closed, leaving no time to measure its running cost before we went to press. Under our standing rule, a unit that completes only part of the program is published with a provisional standing and may be rated again if its maker returns it.
The full grid appears opposite.
Test samples are bought at ordinary retail prices by this magazine unless the grid states otherwise.
----------------------
This Year's Ratings: Small-Office Copiers
Criterion	TN-415	ZR-88	VC-350	LP-620
Running cost per page	Good	Good	Excellent	Not rated
Output quality	Excellent	Good	Good	Excellent
Speed	Good	Excellent	Fair	Good
Reliability in daily use	Excellent	Good	Excellent	Good
Overall standing	2nd	3rd	1st	4th
Test sample	Retail purchase	Maker's demonstration unit	Retail purchase	Retail purchase
Weeks in test	10	10	4	3
Status	Full rating	Full rating	Full rating, short run only	Provisional, running cost not measured
----------------------
Following our small-office copier comparison in the March issue
Readers Ask
The maker of the LP-620 sent it back to you. Has its place in the grid changed? — from an office administrator
It has. The unit ran the complete program in April, and its running cost was measured for the first time, falling in the middle band. With all four criteria scored, the provisional entry is withdrawn, and the LP-620 now stands third, ahead of the ZR-88.
We copy customer documents all day, and running cost is not our concern. Where in the grid should we look? — from a print-room supervisor
Do not start with the standing row, which is led by the unit that is cheapest to run. Choose the model that took the top band for output quality and also for reliability in daily use, and that stayed in the test the full ten weeks.
— N. Pilcher, Equipment Testing Editor
Send further questions to our testing desk.

Plots | Charges | Enrolling | Rules
Plots and Placement
Plots come in three categories: compact, standard, and double. Growers who held a plot last season keep their current category. Applicants new to the program are placed only after walking the site with the plot coordinator, who assigns a category from the space then available.

One payment of $60 applies to every category and covers water at the taps, one compost delivery, and use of the shared tool shed. Oakvale Business Journal — Workplace
"We Would Rather Fill the Room," Says Braddock Instruments
By Naomi Trask, Westbourne
Beginning next month, the staff dining room at Braddock Instruments will sell midday meals to people employed by other businesses in the district. The arrangement will run as a trial.
The room, which seats 240, has been open only to the company's own workforce since it opened. A renovation completed two years ago replaced the furniture and lighting, but it added no seats.
"Many of our production employees now divide the week between the plant and their homes, so our tables stand half empty at noon," said Bridget Ellsworth, the company's catering manager. "We would rather fill the room, and we hope word spreads among nearby offices."
Visitors from other firms may enter from 12:45 P.M. until midday service closes at 2:00 P.M. The earlier stretch is not open to them, because that is when employees arrive in the greatest numbers. Meals will cost visitors $6 to $9, paid at a self-service point rather than charged to an employer. Service hours themselves are unchanged, and meal arrangements for Braddock Instruments employees are not affected.
The trial will run for six months, and the review outcome will be posted on the company's website.

"Many of our production employees now divide the week between the plant and their homes, so our tables stand half empty at noon," said Bridget Ellsworth, the company's catering manager. "We would rather fill the room, and we hope word spreads among nearby offices."
Visitors from other firms may enter from 12:45 P.M. until midday service closes at 2:00 P.M. The earlier stretch is not open to them, because that is when employees arrive in the greatest numbers. Meals will cost visitors $6 to $9, paid at a self-service point rather than charged to an employer. Service hours themselves are unchanged, and meal arrangements for Braddock Instruments employees are not affected.
The trial will run for six months, and the review outcome will be posted on the company's website.

Diego Mercado, 10:01 A.M.: It is on the top shelf in the stockroom. I will have it on the counter by half past one.

Fernhill Town Center Traders' Association
Home | News | Shop Directory | For Businesses (current page) | Inquiries
How is the Fernhill Town Voucher accepted and redeemed?
A voucher presented at your counter must be taken at its printed value against any goods in stock, and no part of it may be returned as cash. --[1]--.
What does accepting the voucher bring in?
Vouchers cannot be spent outside the enrolled premises, so the money loaded onto them stays in the district. Every enrolled address appears on the list that goes out with each voucher sold. Bulk orders are placed by local employers for their staff, and many holders have never shopped at the address they choose. --[2]--.
How do collected vouchers become money again?
Keep the vouchers you take in and send them to the association office as one batch each month. A batch is settled only when the printed values in it come to $40 or more, and a smaller batch should be held and sent in with the following month's batch. --[3]--. Batches must reach the office by the tenth day of the month, as the office makes its payments in one run shortly afterward, and a late batch waits for the next run. Vouchers sent in are not returned.
What is supplied for the counter and window?
Three items are sent to a store when it joins: a window sticker, a small counter card, and a printed note that explains the voucher to shoppers who ask about it. The sticker is to be shown in the window, where it can be read from the street. --[4]--.
Page last revised on 6 February. Anything not covered here should be put to the association office.

Fernhill Town Center Traders' Association
Home | News | Shop Directory | For Businesses (current page) | Inquiries
How is the Fernhill Town Voucher accepted and redeemed?
A voucher presented at your counter must be taken at its printed value against any goods in stock, and no part of it may be returned as cash. --[1]--.
What does accepting the voucher bring in?
Vouchers cannot be spent outside the enrolled premises, so the money loaded onto them stays in the district. Every enrolled address appears on the list that goes out with each voucher sold. Bulk orders are placed by local employers for their staff, and many holders have never shopped at the address they choose. --[2]--.
How do collected vouchers become money again?
Keep the vouchers you take in and send them to the association office as one batch each month. A batch is settled only when the printed values in it come to $40 or more, and a smaller batch should be held and sent in with the following month's batch. --[3]--. Batches must reach the office by the tenth day of the month, as the office makes its payments in one run shortly afterward, and a late batch waits for the next run. Vouchers sent in are not returned.
What is supplied for the counter and window?
Three items are sent to a store when it joins: a window sticker, a small counter card, and a printed note that explains the voucher to shoppers who ask about it. The sticker is to be shown in the window, where it can be read from the street. --[4]--.
